---
title: "3. Modern Causal Machine Learning"
---

::: {.module-meta}
**Duration:** 12 weeks  
**Outcome:** Estimate heterogeneous causal effects and learn treatment policies with modern ML.
:::

## Core topics

Potential outcomes; orthogonal scores; cross-fitting; DML; meta-learners; causal forests; CATE; policy learning.

## Essential resources

- Chernozhukov, V., et al. (2018). Double/debiased machine learning for treatment and structural parameters. *The Econometrics Journal, 21*(1), C1–C68.
- Athey, S., Tibshirani, J., & Wager, S. (2019). Generalized random forests. *Annals of Statistics, 47*(2), 1148–1178.
- Athey, S., & Wager, S. (2021). Policy learning with observational data. *Econometrica, 89*(1), 133–161.
- *Applied Causal Inference Powered by ML and AI* — <https://causalml-book.org/>
- Stanford GSB **Machine Learning & Causal Inference** — <https://www.gsb.stanford.edu/faculty-research/labs-initiatives/sil/research/methods/ai-machine-learning/short-course>

## Milestone

Estimate ATE, ATT and CATE using conventional econometrics, DML, meta-learners and causal forests; then estimate a treatment policy.
